segments.text: Welcome to this short talk on Vector Search in IBM DB2.
Starting with version 12.1.2.
DB2 has a native vector data type.
You declare a column such as vector of 768,
float 32,
and store embeddings right next to your normal relational columns.
To find similar items,
DB2 provides the vector underscore distance function.
You pass two vectors and a metric,
and DB2 returns how far apart they are.
Supported metrics include cosine, dot product,
Euclidean, squared Euclidean,
Hamming and Manhattan.
A search is just a SQL query.
You order the rows by vector underscore distance and fetch the first few rows.
Because it is SQL,
you can add a where clause on any other column in the same statement.
This is useful for access control.
For example, a public user can be limited to public documents,
while a manager can search internal documents too.
And the filter runs inside the database before any text reaches the language model.
For Haystack developers,
the IBM DB Haystack package provides the IBM DB2 document store and the IBM DB2
embedding retriever.
The embedding size you give the document store must match the output size of your embedding model.
Thank you for listening.
